advances: Proves the all-tilt cubic moment estimate for complete ternary cubes with the absolute coefficient \(\kappa=1/64\). The mechanism uses actual ambient halfspace caps, exposed faces, and antipodal reflection, rather than a lossless induction through ternary layers. This class result does not establish the locked mixed-integer target or the analogous estimate on all complete lattice supports.
author: research-agent
proof:
All probabilities and depths in this proof have the normalizations in the statement; no accepted predecessor is required.

First establish the exact exposed-face identity. A closed ambient halfspace containing \(\mathbf z\), when its defining inequality is expressed in the free coordinates of \(F_{\mathbf z}\), defines either a closed halfspace containing \(\mathbf0\) or the whole free-coordinate space. Its conditional mass is therefore at least \(\tau_{q_I}(\mathbf0)\). For \(k=0\), its face intersection contains the singleton \(\mathbf z\), and the same assertion holds with the stated convention. Consequently every such ambient halfspace has mass at least \(\alpha_{\mathbf z}\tau_{q_I}(\mathbf0)\). Taking the minimum gives the lower inequality needed for the first identity in (2).

For the reverse inequality, suppose first that \(k\ge1\). There are finitely many traces of halfspaces on the finite conditional support, so an intrinsic minimizing cap exists. Write a minimizing cap as \(\{\mathbf x:\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf x\ge b\}\), where \(\mathbf a\ne\mathbf0\) and \(b\le0\). Replacing \(b\) by \(0\) gives a contained admissible cap through \(\mathbf0\), so this new cap is also minimizing. Regard \(\mathbf a\) as an ambient vector whose coordinates on \(J\) vanish.

Define an ambient vector \(\mathbf b_{\mathbf z}\) by \((b_{\mathbf z})_i=z_i\) for \(i\in J\) and \((b_{\mathbf z})_i=0\) for \(i\in I\). For every \(\mathbf x\in D\),
\[
\mathbf b_{\mathbf z}\cdot(\mathbf x-\mathbf z)
=\sum_{i\in J}(z_i x_i-1)\le0.
\tag{3}
\]
Equality holds exactly on \(D\cap F_{\mathbf z}\); outside that face, the expression is an integer at most \(-1\). In particular, when \(J\ne\varnothing\), this vector exposes \(F_{\mathbf z}\).

Choose a real \(L>\sum_{i\in I}|a_i|\). The single ambient closed halfspace
\[
H=\{\mathbf u:(\mathbf a+L\mathbf b_{\mathbf z})\cdot(\mathbf u-\mathbf z)\ge0\}
\tag{4}
\]
contains \(\mathbf z\). On the face, its trace is exactly the chosen intrinsic minimizing cap, since \(z_i=0\) on \(I\). Outside the face, (3) and \(|\mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf x-\mathbf z)|\le\sum_{i\in I}|a_i|\) make the left side of (4) strictly negative. If \(J=\varnothing\), the face is the whole cube and (4) is simply the intrinsic minimizing cap. The normal in (4) is nonzero: \(\mathbf a\ne\mathbf0\), and the two summands have disjoint coordinate supports. Thus (4) is an actual ambient halfspace of mass exactly \(\alpha_{\mathbf z}\tau_{q_I}(\mathbf0)\).

If \(k=0\), then \(J=\{1,\ldots,N\}\) and \(\mathbf b_{\mathbf z}=\mathbf z\ne\mathbf0\). Equation (3) shows that the halfspace \(\{\mathbf u:\mathbf b_{\mathbf z}\cdot(\mathbf u-\mathbf z)\ge0\}\) intersects \(D\) only at \(\mathbf z\). It has mass \(p_{\mathbf z}=\alpha_{\mathbf z}\). This proves the first identity in (2), including the exact vertex depths. The construction is a single containing halfspace, not an intersection of coordinate halfspaces.

Next establish the count and reflection estimate independently. Suppose \(k\ge1\), and let \(A\) be the trace of any closed halfspace in \(\mathbb R^I\) containing \(\mathbf0\). Write the halfspace as \(\{\mathbf x:\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf x\ge b\}\) with \(b\le0\). The nonzero sites of \(\{-1,0,1\}^{I}\) split into \((3^k-1)/2\) distinct antipodal pairs \(\{\mathbf x,-\mathbf x\}\). At least one point of each pair satisfies \(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf x\ge0\) and hence belongs to \(A\); the center also belongs to \(A\). Therefore \(|A|\ge(3^k+1)/2\). If the boundary is through \(\mathbf0\) and \(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf x\ne0\) at every nonzero site, exactly one point of each pair belongs, giving the asserted equality. Such normals exist: after ordering the \(k\) free coordinates, take their coefficients to be \(1,3,\ldots,3^{k-1}\). At any nonzero site the highest nonzero coordinate contributes a magnitude strictly greater than the sum of all preceding magnitudes.

Reflection preserves the conditional support and gives the exact identity
\[
q_I(\mathbf x)q_I(-\mathbf x)
=\frac1{\bigl(\prod_{i\in I}Z_i\bigr)^2}.
\]
Applying Cauchy--Schwarz on \(A\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{|A|^2}{\bigl(\prod_{i\in I}Z_i\bigr)^2}
&=\left(\sum_{\mathbf x\in A}\sqrt{q_I(\mathbf x)q_I(-\mathbf x)}\right)^2\\
&\le\left(\sum_{\mathbf x\in A}q_I(\mathbf x)\right)
\left(\sum_{\mathbf x\in A}q_I(-\mathbf x)\right)\\
&=q_I(A)q_I(-A)\le q_I(A).
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
The final inequality uses only that \(-A\) is a subset of the conditional support and has probability at most \(1\). There is no deletion of boundary sites and no assertion that the two probabilities are independent. The count and (5) show
\[
q_I(A)\ge\frac{(3^k+1)^2}{4\bigl(\prod_{i\in I}Z_i\bigr)^2}
\ge\frac{3^{2k}}{4\bigl(\prod_{i\in I}Z_i\bigr)^2}.
\]
Taking the minimum proves the second inequality in (2) for \(k\ge1\). For \(k=0\), that inequality reads \(1\ge1/4\), so it holds as well.

For the all-root sum, the root probability is \(p_{\mathbf z}=\alpha_{\mathbf z}/\prod_{i\in I}Z_i\). Thus (2) gives, for every root including vertices,
\[
\begin{aligned}
p_{\mathbf z}\tau_p(\mathbf z)^3
&\ge\frac1{64}\,\alpha_{\mathbf z}^4
\frac{3^{6k}}{\bigl(\prod_{i\in I}Z_i\bigr)^7}\\
&=\frac1{64}
\prod_{i\in J}\frac{e^{4\theta_i z_i}}{Z_i^4}
\prod_{i\in I}\frac{729}{Z_i^7}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
Summing (6) over all \(\mathbf z\in\{-1,0,1\}^N\) factors into the product in the first inequality of (1). Each coordinate contributes \(e^{4\theta_i}/Z_i^4\), \(e^{-4\theta_i}/Z_i^4\), or \(729/Z_i^7\), according as its root coordinate is \(1\), \(-1\), or \(0\). In fact the exact vertex depths give the stronger bound
\[
M_3(p)\ge\frac1{64}
\prod_{i=1}^N\left(
\frac{e^{4\theta_i}+e^{-4\theta_i}}{Z_i^4}
+\frac{729}{Z_i^7}
\right)
+\frac{63}{64}\prod_{i=1}^N\frac{e^{4\theta_i}+e^{-4\theta_i}}{Z_i^4},
\tag{7}
\]
because (6) charged only \(1/64\) of the exact contribution of every vertex. The additional term in (7) is nonnegative and is not needed below.

It remains to prove the scalar inequality for every real tilt, with no numerical minimization. Fix \(\theta\in\mathbb R\), put \(r=e^\theta+e^{-\theta}=2\cosh\theta\ge2\), and note that \(Z=r+1\) and \(e^{4\theta}+e^{-4\theta}=r^4-4r^2+2\). Hence the desired scalar bound is equivalent to
\[
\frac{r^4-4r^2+2}{(r+1)^4}+\frac{729}{(r+1)^7}\ge\frac18,
\]
or, after multiplication by the positive number \(8(r+1)^7\), to
\[
8(r^4-4r^2+2)(r+1)^3+5832-(r+1)^7\ge0.
\tag{8}
\]
Set \(s=r-2\ge0\). Direct multiplication gives the following exact polynomial identity for the left side of (8):
\[
\begin{aligned}
&8(r^4-4r^2+2)(r+1)^3+5832-(r+1)^7\\
&\quad=7s^7+115s^6+763s^5+2567s^4+4381s^3
+2817s^2-1215s+4077\\
&\quad=7s^7+115s^6+763s^5+2567s^4+4381s^3
+1602s^2+1215(s^2-s+1)+2862.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
Every term in the last line is nonnegative for \(s\ge0\), and \(s^2-s+1=(s-1/2)^2+3/4>0\). Thus (8) holds strictly for every \(r\ge2\). Applying this scalar estimate to each factor in (1) proves \(M_3(p)\ge(1/64)8^{-N}\), as claimed.
statement:
For every integer \(N\ge1\) and every \(\boldsymbol\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_N)\in\mathbb R^N\), let \(D=\{-1,0,1\}^N\), let \(Z_i=1+e^{\theta_i}+e^{-\theta_i}\), and define the strictly positive probability law
\[
p_{\mathbf z}=\prod_{i=1}^N\frac{e^{\theta_i z_i}}{Z_i}
\qquad(\mathbf z\in D).
\]
Use the canonical normalized actual closed-halfspace depth and cubic moment:
\[
\tau_p(\mathbf z)=\min_{\substack{H\subseteq\mathbb R^N\text{ a closed halfspace}\\\mathbf z\in H}}
\sum_{\mathbf x\in D\cap H}p_{\mathbf x},
\qquad
M_3(p)=\sum_{\mathbf z\in D}p_{\mathbf z}\tau_p(\mathbf z)^3.
\]
Then
\[
M_3(p)\ge\frac1{64}
\prod_{i=1}^N\left(
\frac{e^{4\theta_i}+e^{-4\theta_i}}{Z_i^4}
+\frac{729}{Z_i^7}
\right)
\ge\frac1{64}\,8^{-N}.
\tag{1}
\]
In particular, the same coefficient \(\kappa=1/64\) works for every \(N\) and all tilt parameters. The support is full-dimensional and complete, since its convex hull is \([-1,1]^N\) and \([-1,1]^N\cap\mathbb Z^N=D\).

The pointwise mechanism behind (1) is exact at exposed faces. For a root \(\mathbf z\in D\), put \(I=\{i:z_i=0\}\), \(J=\{1,\ldots,N\}\setminus I\), and \(k=|I|\). Let
\[
F_{\mathbf z}=\{\mathbf u\in[-1,1]^N:u_i=z_i\text{ for every }i\in J\},
\qquad
\alpha_{\mathbf z}=p(F_{\mathbf z})=\prod_{i\in J}\frac{e^{\theta_i z_i}}{Z_i}.
\]
The conditional law on its free coordinates is
\[
q_I(\mathbf x)=\frac{\exp\bigl(\sum_{i\in I}\theta_i x_i\bigr)}{\prod_{i\in I}Z_i}
\qquad(\mathbf x\in\{-1,0,1\}^{I}).
\]
For \(k\ge1\), \(\tau_{q_I}(\mathbf0)\) is the actual closed-halfspace depth in \(\mathbb R^{I}\); for \(I=\varnothing\), define it to be \(1\), the mass of the singleton conditional support. With empty products equal to \(1\), one has
\[
\tau_p(\mathbf z)=\alpha_{\mathbf z}\tau_{q_I}(\mathbf0),
\qquad
\tau_{q_I}(\mathbf0)\ge
\frac{3^{2k}}{4\bigl(\prod_{i\in I}Z_i\bigr)^2}.
\tag{2}
\]
Thus every vertex \(\mathbf z\in\{-1,1\}^N\) has exactly \(\tau_p(\mathbf z)=p_{\mathbf z}\), not merely the weaker bound obtained by applying the second inequality in (2) with \(k=0\). Moreover, for every \(k\ge1\), a cap through \(\mathbf0\) whose boundary contains no other point of \(\{-1,0,1\}^{I}\) has exactly \((3^k+1)/2\) supported sites. Every containing cap, including nongeneric caps and their boundary atoms, contains at least that many.
